 Friday, November 20 Los Angeles, Calif. 10 p.m. CT Baylor
 vs Southern California
 Buy Tickets Game Coverage: Listen Live Stats WBB Faces Stiff Test at No. 4/5 Southern California on Friday Night
 11/18/2026 4:12:00 PM | Women's Basketball
 Baylor Notes (PDF) Share: WACO, Texas –  Baylor plays its first road game of the 2026-27 season on Friday, traveling to Los Angeles to face No. 4/5 Southern California at 10 p.m. CT at the Intuit Dome. The game will air on Big Ten Network and the Baylor Sports Media Network.
Baylor (5-0) faces Southern Cal (3-1) in a clash on the Big Ten Network, which will be called by Krista Blunk (play-by-play) and Shimmy Gray-Miller (analyst). The game will also air on the Baylor Sports Media Network, live locally on 93.9 FM and on BaylorBears.com and CenTexSportsFan.com, with the Voice of the Bears, Derek Smith (play-by-play) and Lori Fogleman (analyst) on the call. 
The Bears will play two games more than 1,200 miles apart in a 40-hour span this weekend, returning home following the USC game to play host to Northern Kentucky on Sunday at 2 p.m. at Foster Pavilion.   
Baylor and USC meet for the fourth time in the history of the two programs with the Trojans leading the all-time series 2-1. The last time they faced off, No. 1 seed Southern California defeated the Bears 74-70 in the 2024 NCAA Tournament Sweet 16 at the Moda Center in Portland. 
Baylor is the third Big 12 team this century to score at least 100 points in three consecutive games, joining the Bears' own 2013-14 squad and last year's Oklahoma State team. Eclipsing the 100-point mark on Friday would make Baylor the first Big 12 team to do so in four consecutive games in the 21st century.
Baylor is receiving votes in both the AP and  USA Today  coaches polls. Southern California is ranked No. 4 in the AP poll and No. 5 in the  USA Today  Coaches poll. The Bears are 178-92 against Top 25 opponents since 2000 and last defeated a top-10 team on January 4, 2026, downing #10 Iowa State. 
 HOW THEY'RE STACKING UP 
• Baylor ranks in the national top 25 in 11 team categories through Nov. 17 and leads the Big 12 in eight of them. The Bears are first nationally in winning percentage (100%) and second in defensive rebounds per game (34.4).
• Baylor is third nationally in bench points per game (42.0) and fourth in both field goal percentage (54.7%) and scoring margin (+46.6). The Bears are also sixth in scoring offense (98.4), eighth in three point percentage (42.5%), eighth in assists per game (22.4), 10th in rebounds per game (48.6) and 23rd in assist-to-turnover ratio (+1.49).
• Taliah Scott is first nationally and in the Big 12 in free throw percentage at 100%.
• Trinity Turner leads the nation in assists (42) and is second nationally in assists per game (8.4), while ranking first in the Big 12 in both categories. 
• Kate Koval and Kayla Nelms both rank in the top-20 nationally in double-doubles. Koval is second in the nation and first in the Big 12 with three double dips, while Nelms is 20th nationally and second in the Big 12 with two. 
• Koval is 18th in the country and second in the Big 12 in total rebounds with 51, while leading the league and ranking 25th nationally in rebounds per game at 10.2.
• Nelms checks in at 18th nationally and second in the Big 12 in field goal percentage at 66.7%.
• Tianna Thompson is seventh nationally and first in the Big 12 in 3-point percentage (64.0%). She is ninth nationally in 3-pointers made (16) and 19th in 3-pointers per game (3.20).
 RETURN OF THE "PROFESSIONAL SCORER" 
• Taliah Scott returns to Baylor for another season after an introductory year in green and gold in which she averaged 19.7 points per game and landed all over the program's single-season top 10: tied for third in 3-pointers made, first in 3-pointers attempted, fifth in free throws made, tied for eighth in free throws attempted and first in free throw percentage (89.5%). 
• This week, she was named to the Preseason Top 50 Watch List for the 2027 John R. Wooden Award. She had already been named to the preseason watch lists for the Ann Meyers Drysdale Shooting Guard Award and the Naismith Trophy. 
• The Jacksonville, Fla., native accounted for 27% of the Bears' offense last season and ranked second in the Big 12 in scoring. 
• Scott led Baylor in scoring in 27 of 33 games in 2025-26 and scored in double figures 30 times, including her first double-double (23 points, 10 assists) against Southeastern Louisiana. 
• She reached 1,000 career points in her 48th game in early 2026, averaging 21.1 points at the time. She became the 22nd Division I player since 2000 to hit the mark in 48 games or fewer, tying for the 19th-fewest games needed.
• Scott earned numerous postseason honors, including Women's Basketball Coaches Association honorable mention All-America and All-Big 12 first team.
 THE HELPING HAND 
• Point guard Trinity Turner , who arrived at Baylor this summer from Georgia, leads the nation with 42 assists (8.4 per game) through five games of the 2026-27 season.
• She also has an assist-to-turnover ratio of +4.20, which is top-five in the Big 12 and among the top-35 nationally.
• Turner's 21 assists in her first two games were the most by a Big 12 newcomer through two games this century. She was also the fifth player since 2000 to record at least 10 assists in her debut with a Big 12 team.
• Against Central Arkansas, she recorded her second career double-double with a career-high 11 assists, 13 points and nine rebounds, one rebound shy of a triple-double. She shot 6-of-16 from the field and made one 3-pointer.
